turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, good afternoon. I have brought my husband. He will say he is perfectly fine, but I am not happy with how things are.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I am fine. You dragged me from my nap. I am tired, so please be quick.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): One second, the screen has stuck... okay, it is back. What is worrying you?
[SEG0004] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He keeps repeating questions, and he forgot two clinic appointments.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I did not forget. The clinic changed the time and nobody told me properly. She is exaggerating.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, repeat that? I clicked the wrong window. He forgot two appointments, is that what you are saying?
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. I wrote both dates on the calendar and he still did not go. He forgot.
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And sometime last month he got lost coming back from the vegetable market, ten minutes from home. I cannot remember the exact day.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not lost. The road was dug up so I took the side lane. Stop making a drama.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long with the repeated questions? Say it again, I was typing.
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was about to say six months. No, it is eight months. Four or five times a day he asks what day it is, or whether the maid has come.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I ask one time. You don't listen. Don't hang eight months on me.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fall, or any hit on the head?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No falls and no head injury. I am with him most of the day.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I am only tired, and my sleep is bad. I wake up and then I cannot sleep again.
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): True, that part. He is up around three in the morning and then he dozes all afternoon.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever, chest pain, weight loss? I have to ask again, I did not hear an answer.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no chest pain. Weight is the same. I am not shrinking.
[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His trousers are loose since about two months. He refuses the scale, so there is no number.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The trousers are old. I have not lost weight. That is enough.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): The tablet list on this system is old. Please go through what he actually takes, slowly.
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I manage all the medicines. Amlodipine for BP, in the morning, by mouth, five milligrams.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): It is ten milligrams. I have been on ten for years. She does not know.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The strip at home is five milligrams. I will not agree to ten. We can bring it and show you.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): So that dose is unclear. What is the next tablet? I only half heard.
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Metformin five hundred milligrams twice a day, by mouth, with food, for the sugar. I hand it to him, so that one is not missed.
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ecosprin seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty milligrams, once daily after food, by mouth. The cardiologist increased it. I said the old dose by mistake.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hundred and fifty, not seventy-five. I have corrected it here. What about night time?
[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Atorvastatin forty milligrams at night, by mouth, for cholesterol. If he has already fallen asleep I skip that one sometimes.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): There was a sleeping tablet also. I took it once. She stopped it after that.
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Alprazolam. It was written as point five milligrams... no, point two five. One tablet by mouth in March, he was drowsy the whole next day, and I stopped it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stopped after the one dose. Anything that was suggested and never started?
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Citicoline syrup. Another doctor suggested it. We never bought it, he never took a drop. I wanted you to see him first.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergy, or food allergy?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing at all.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long for the BP and the sugar?
[SEG0037] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): BP for ten years, ongoing. Diabetes for eight years, also ongoing. When I say sugar I mean diabetes.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): So known hypertension and known diabetes, both still ongoing. Any operation in the past?
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cataract surgery in both eyes... no, only the right eye, three years ago. They said the left can wait.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the right eye, yes. That one is correct.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family side, the parents? Sorry, say it clearly, this letter is not saving and I got distracted.
[SEG0042] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His father had diabetes and died of a stroke. His mother had no major illness.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Smoking, alcohol, and who does he live with?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped smoking twenty years back. I do not drink. I live with my wife. I retired from the bank, accounts department.
[SEG0045] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He used to take a small whisky. He stopped that about five years ago. He stays home with me. He has given up his evening walks, he only goes to the market.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vitals, before the monitor blanks. Blood pressure one forty two over eighty eight... no, one fifty two over eighty eight. Pulse seventy eight... refreshed, it is seventy six.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): You look tired. Face is symmetrical, no weakness there. Speech is clear, and you know you are in the clinic. I am not doing a long memory quiz while you are irritated.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stomach, urine, joints — any problem in those?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not putting a diagnosis on this today. I will arrange bloods — full blood count, HbA1c, kidney function, TSH and vitamin B12 — for treatable causes, and I will arrange a memory assessment.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in six weeks with the reports.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he becomes more confused or gets lost again, come back sooner and do not wait.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do not go to the market alone until the memory assessment is done. Bring the amlodipine strip next time. I am not fixing that dose today.

spec.situation: Spouse brings an older person who 'is fine' but repeats questions, forgets appointments and got lost; patient disagrees on many points; medicines managed by spouse; doctor plans bloods and a memory assessment, no diagnosis said aloud.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Father died of a stroke; transcript does not clearly state father had prior stroke diagnosis.

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose is disputed: family member reports 5 mg orally each morning, patient reports 10 mg, and the doctor explicitly did not resolve or change the dose today pending review of the strip.
Ecosprin indication was stated as increased by the cardiologist.
Citicoline syrup was suggested by another doctor but was never started and never purchased.
Patient denied weight loss ('weight is the same'), despite family member reporting loose trousers.
Doctor stated he was not assigning a diagnosis today.

bad.text: Poor sleep (category=neurological, status=present, frequency=awake around three in the morning and dozes in the afternoon, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose as stated by the family member was 5 mg by mouth each morning; the recorded medication entry omits the dose, and there was an unresolved discrepancy because the patient stated 10 mg.

Weight loss was specifically asked about and the patient denied it ('Weight is the same'); only loose trousers/possible weight loss dispute was recorded, but the direct negative finding for weight loss is missing.
No medicine allergy or food allergy was reported; the recorded negative finding only says 'Allergies' absent, without the spoken detail that both medication and food allergies were denied.

Atorvastatin adherence issue: the family member said she sometimes skips the 40 mg night dose if he has already fallen asleep. This was recorded only as an uncertainty, not as part of the medication history.
Citicoline syrup was suggested by another doctor but was never started and never taken. This planned/considered medication history is missing.
Doctor stated he was not making a diagnosis today. This plan/uncertainty is missing.
